hints: Integrate $x$ with respect to $y$ from $y = 0$ to $y = \frac{3}{2}$.
walkthrough:
Express $x$ as a function of $y$:
$$y = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{x} \implies 2y = \sqrt{x} \implies x = 4y^2$$

Set up the definite integral for the area bounded between the curve and the $y$-axis from $y = 0$ to $y = \frac{3}{2}$:
$$\text{Area} = \int_0^{3/2} 4y^2\,dy = \left[\frac{4}{3}y^3\right]_0^{3/2}$$

Evaluate the antiderivative at the limits:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{4}{3}\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^3 - 0 = \frac{4}{3}\left(\frac{27}{8}\right) = \frac{9}{2} = 4.5$$

hints: Use the volume of revolution formula about the $y$-axis: $V = \pi \int x^2\,dy$.
walkthrough:
Apply the volume of revolution formula about the $y$-axis:
$$V = \pi \int_0^{3/2} x^2\,dy$$

Evaluate the integral at the upper limit $y = \frac{3}{2}$:
$$V = 16\pi \left[\frac{1}{5}\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^5\right] = 16\pi \left(\frac{243}{160}\right) = \frac{243\pi}{10} = 24.3\pi$$
